title: Release of Toxic Gd3+ Ions to Tumour Cells by Vitamin B12 Bioconjugates

synthesis.procedure: DTPA–CNCbl was first prepared by stirring CNCbl (300 mg, 0.22 mmol) and DTPA dianhydride (300 mg, 0.84 mmol) in anhydrous DMSO (40 mL) and anhydrous pyridine (5 mL) for 24 h at 45 °C, followed by aqueous work-up, phenol extraction, Dowex 1×2-400 chromatography (water then 1.0 M NaCl), desalting, and lyophilisation (185 mg, 49%). Complex 1 was then prepared in situ by treating aqueous solutions of DTPA–CNCbl with GdCl3 (0.9 equiv) in water at the desired pH and concentration. Solutions were used immediately or stored frozen to avoid ester hydrolysis.
synthesis.temperature: ligand esterification 45 °C; complexation at ambient aqueous conditions (not further specified)
synthesis.time: 24 h for DTPA–CNCbl esterification; complex 1 prepared immediately prior to use
synthesis.ph: desired pH (not numerically specified for in situ complexation)

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: DTPA–CNCbl isolated by filtration, phenol extraction, Dowex chromatography, desalting, and lyophilisation; 1 not isolated as a solid (used as aqueous solutions)
synthesis.yield: DTPA–CNCbl 185 mg (49%); yield of 1 not reported

properties.summary: 1 is a paramagnetic Gd–DTPA–cobalamin conjugate whose ester hydrolysis was followed by water-proton relaxivity. At 20 MHz and 298 K the millimolar relaxivity is 5.7 mM−1 s−1; in PBS (pH 7.2) r1p falls to 4.7 mM−1 s−1 after 5 h (first-order hydrolysis rate constant (4.7±3)×10−3 min−1), consistent with release of Gd–DTPA.

synthesis.procedure: The dimeric form was obtained by recrystallising 1 with excess GdCl3 (Gd3+:1 = 1.3:1) by hanging-drop vapour diffusion at 293 K. Complex 1 (100 mM, 1 µL) was mixed with reservoir solution (40% v/v PEG 400 and 3.4 M LiCl, 1 µL). Small biconvex-lens crystals formed within hours and some grew over about a week to ~0.25 × 0.1 × 0.05 mm. X-ray data were collected at 100 K.

synthesis.procedure: TTHA–CNCbl was synthesised analogously to DTPA–CNCbl from CNCbl and TTHA dianhydride (yield 120 mg, 30%). Complex 2 was then prepared in situ by the same procedure as 1, treating aqueous TTHA–CNCbl with GdCl3 (0.9 equiv) in water.

properties.summary: 2 is the more coordinatively saturated TTHA analogue. At 20 MHz and 298 K its millimolar relaxivity is 3.1 mM−1 s−1, close to Gd–TTHA (2.5 mM−1 s−1), and hydrolysis of the ester is much slower than for 1.
